import os
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import duckdb
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

os.makedirs("out", exist_ok=True)

df = duckdb.sql("""
SELECT year(crash_date) AS year,
       count(*) AS reported_crashes,
       sum(number_of_persons_injured) AS persons_injured,
       sum(number_of_persons_killed) AS persons_killed,
       sum(number_of_motorist_injured) AS motorist_injured,
       sum(number_of_motorist_killed) AS motorist_killed,
       sum(number_of_pedestrians_killed) AS pedestrian_killed,
       sum(number_of_cyclist_killed) AS cyclist_killed
FROM 'data/crashes.parquet'
WHERE crash_date BETWEEN DATE '2013-01-01' AND DATE '2025-12-31'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1
""").df()

base = float(df.loc[df.year == 2013, "motorist_killed"].iloc[0])
last = float(df.loc[df.year == 2025, "motorist_killed"].iloc[0])
ratio = last / base

# Miles driven is not in the data, so express deaths as an index holding VMT flat
# (not a per-mile quantity; rename per reviewer issue 3).
df["motorist_deaths_index_flat_vmt"] = df["motorist_killed"] / base * 100.0
df["motorist_deaths_per_1000_crashes"] = df["motorist_killed"] / df["reported_crashes"] * 1000

df.to_csv("out/revised_values.csv", index=False)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 5.5))

a = ax[0]
a.bar(df.year, df.motorist_killed, color="#4C72B0", label="Motorist deaths (occupants)")
a.plot(df.year, df.persons_killed, "o-", color="#C44E52", lw=1.5, ms=4,
       label="All road-user deaths")
a.annotate(f"{int(base)}", (2013, base), textcoords="offset points", xytext=(0, 8),
           ha="center", fontsize=10, fontweight="bold")
a.annotate(f"{int(last)}", (2025, last), textcoords="offset points", xytext=(0, 8),
           ha="center", fontsize=10, fontweight="bold")
a.set_title("Motor vehicle deaths per year, NYC (crash reports)")
a.set_ylabel("Deaths per year")
a.set_xticks(list(df.year))
a.tick_params(axis="x", rotation=60)
a.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.3)
a.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=9)

b = ax[1]
vmt = np.linspace(0.60, 1.20, 241)
risk = (ratio) / vmt * 100.0
b.plot(vmt * 100, risk, color="#4C72B0", lw=2,
       label="2025 risk vs 2013 risk (index)")
b.axhline(100, color="black", ls="--", lw=1, label="No change (100)")
# Color spans to track the risk outcome: below break-even (74%) risk rises; above, it falls
b.axvspan(60, ratio * 100, color="#C44E52", alpha=0.12)
b.axvspan(ratio * 100, 120, color="#55A868", alpha=0.12)
b.plot([100], [ratio * 100], "o", color="#C44E52", ms=8)
b.annotate(f"miles flat: {ratio*100:.0f}\n(risk -{100-ratio*100:.0f}%)",
           (100, ratio * 100), textcoords="offset points", xytext=(12, 6),
           fontsize=9, color="#C44E52")
b.plot([ratio * 100], [100], "o", color="black", ms=7)
b.annotate(f"break-even\n{ratio*100:.0f}%", (ratio * 100, 100),
           textcoords="offset points", xytext=(-6, -34), ha="right", fontsize=9)
b.text(61.5, 168, "risk rises", color="#C44E52", fontsize=9, fontweight="bold")
b.text(102, 168, "risk falls", color="#55A868", fontsize=9, fontweight="bold")
b.set_title("2025 vs 2013 motorist risk per mile,\nfor different assumptions about miles driven")
b.set_xlabel("Miles driven in 2025 as % of 2013")
b.set_ylabel("Risk per mile, 2025 = % of 2013")
b.set_xlim(60, 120)
b.set_ylim(55, 180)
b.grid(alpha=0.3)
b.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=9, loc="upper right")

fig.suptitle("Did the risk of a motorist being killed per mile driven fall in NYC, 2013-2025?",
             fontsize=13, fontweight="bold")
fig.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.94])
fig.savefig("out/revised.png", dpi=150)

print(df.to_string(index=False))
print(f"2013 motorist deaths: {base:.0f}, 2025: {last:.0f}, change: {last/base*100-100:.1f}%")
print(f"Break-even VMT ratio 2025/2013: {ratio:.3f}")
print(f"2013 rate/1000 crashes: {base/df.loc[df.year==2013,'reported_crashes'].iloc[0]*1000:.3f}, "
      f"2025: {last/df.loc[df.year==2025,'reported_crashes'].iloc[0]*1000:.3f}")

part.text:
All four issues addressed; numbers and chart structure unchanged. Chart at `out/revised.png`, data at `out/revised_values.csv`.

CHANGES:
1. fixed: Moved the shading boundary from 100% to the break-even miles ratio (~74%): red span (60–74%) is now where risk per mile rises, green (74–120%) where it falls, with in-plot labels "red: risk rises" / "green: risk falls".
2. fixed: Reworded the conclusion as an explicit conditional ("if 2025 mileage is at least ~74% of 2013's, risk per mile fell ~26%") since the data contains no miles-driven measure.
3. fixed: Renamed the column to `motorist_deaths_index_flat_vmt` (deaths index under flat VMT, not a per-mile quantity); same values.
4. fixed: Replaced "injury counts stayed flat" with the accurate statement that injuries fell ~19–20% from 2018–19 levels (61,391/61,940 → 49,634 in 2025), far less than the 60% drop in reported crashes (211,486 → 85,546).

ANSWER: Motorist (vehicle-occupant) deaths fell from 110 in 2013 to 81 in 2025, a 26% drop. Because the data has no miles-driven column, the per-mile question is answered by break-even: the risk of a motorist being killed per mile driven fell if 2025 mileage was at least ~74% of 2013's — in that case risk per mile is about 26% lower than in 2013 (it would rise only if 2025 driving fell below ~74% of 2013 levels). Caveats: the 2020–21 spike in deaths per crash, and the post-2019 halving of minor-crash reports (injuries fell only ~19–20% from 2018–19, far less than the 60% drop in reported crashes), so trends in reports alone overstate the change in exposure.
